requirements.quote: When a Server takes ownership of an incoming Application Message it MUST add it to the Session state of those clients that have matching Subscriptions. Matching rules are defined in Section 4.7 [MQTT-4.5.0-1].
requirements.condition: When a Server takes ownership of an incoming Application Message.
requirements.required_behavior: Add the message to the Session state of every Client whose Subscription matches it under the Section 4.7 matching rules.
requirements.why_checkable: Known Client Sessions and matching Subscriptions can be installed, then their queued Session state inspected after publication.

requirements.quote: The Client MUST acknowledge any Publish Packet it receives according to the applicable QoS rules regardless of whether it elects to process the Application Message that it contains [MQTT-4.5.0-2].
requirements.condition: Whenever a Client receives a Publish Packet, including when it elects not to process the contained Application Message.
requirements.required_behavior: Acknowledge the Publish Packet according to its applicable QoS rules.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Suppress the required acknowledgement solely because the Application Message is not processed.
requirements.why_checkable: A Client can be configured to decline application processing while its protocol acknowledgement traffic is observed.

requirements.quote: When it re-sends any PUBLISH packets, it MUST re-send them in the order in which the original PUBLISH packets were sent (this applies to QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages) [MQTT-4.6.0-1]
requirements.condition: When a Client re-sends multiple QoS 1 PUBLISH packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Re-send them in the order in which their original PUBLISH packets were sent.
requirements.why_checkable: Original and retransmission sequences can be captured and their relative order compared.

requirements.quote: When it re-sends any PUBLISH packets, it MUST re-send them in the order in which the original PUBLISH packets were sent (this applies to QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages) [MQTT-4.6.0-1]
requirements.condition: When a Client re-sends multiple QoS 2 PUBLISH packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Re-send them in the order in which their original PUBLISH packets were sent.
requirements.why_checkable: Original and retransmission sequences can be captured and their relative order compared.

requirements.quote: It MUST send PUBACK packets in the order in which the corresponding PUBLISH packets were received (QoS 1 messages) [MQTT-4.6.0-2]
requirements.condition: When a Client sends PUBACK packets for multiple received QoS 1 PUBLISH packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Send PUBACK packets in the order in which the corresponding PUBLISH packets were received.
requirements.why_checkable: The order of incoming PUBLISH identifiers can be compared with the order of outgoing PUBACK identifiers.

requirements.quote: It MUST send PUBREC packets in the order in which the corresponding PUBLISH packets were received (QoS 2 messages) [MQTT-4.6.0-3]
requirements.condition: When a Client sends PUBREC packets for multiple received QoS 2 PUBLISH packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Send PUBREC packets in the order in which the corresponding PUBLISH packets were received.
requirements.why_checkable: The order of incoming PUBLISH identifiers can be compared with the order of outgoing PUBREC identifiers.

requirements.quote: It MUST send PUBREL packets in the order in which the corresponding PUBREC packets were received (QoS 2 messages) [MQTT-4.6.0-4]
requirements.condition: When a Client sends PUBREL packets after receiving multiple PUBREC packets in QoS 2 flows.
requirements.required_behavior: Send PUBREL packets in the order in which the corresponding PUBREC packets were received.
requirements.why_checkable: Incoming PUBREC identifier order can be compared with outgoing PUBREL identifier order.

requirements.quote: A Server MUST by default treat each Topic as an "Ordered Topic".
requirements.condition: When no configuration explicitly makes a Topic unordered.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat every Topic as an Ordered Topic.
requirements.why_checkable: Message delivery order on an unconfigured Topic can be observed against Ordered Topic rules.

requirements.quote: It MAY provide an administrative or other mechanism to allow one or more Topics to be treated as an "Unordered Topic" [MQTT-4.6.0-5].
requirements.condition: When evaluating whether a Server implements a mechanism for Unordered Topics.
requirements.required_behavior: Provide an optional mechanism that can mark one or more Topics as unordered.
requirements.why_checkable: MAY makes the mechanism entirely optional, so its absence cannot produce a deterministic conformance failure.

requirements.quote: When a Server processes a message that has been published to an Ordered Topic, it MUST follow the rules listed above when delivering messages to each of its subscribers.
requirements.condition: When a Server re-sends multiple QoS 1 PUBLISH packets to a subscriber for an Ordered Topic.
requirements.required_behavior: Re-send them in the order in which their original PUBLISH packets were sent.
requirements.why_checkable: The sentence applies the preceding retransmission-order rule to Server delivery for each subscriber.

requirements.quote: When a Server processes a message that has been published to an Ordered Topic, it MUST follow the rules listed above when delivering messages to each of its subscribers.
requirements.condition: When a Server re-sends multiple QoS 2 PUBLISH packets to a subscriber for an Ordered Topic.
requirements.required_behavior: Re-send them in the order in which their original PUBLISH packets were sent.
requirements.why_checkable: The sentence applies the preceding retransmission-order rule to Server delivery for each subscriber.

requirements.quote: When a Server processes a message that has been published to an Ordered Topic, it MUST follow the rules listed above when delivering messages to each of its subscribers.
requirements.condition: When a Server sends PUBACK packets for multiple QoS 1 PUBLISH packets associated with an Ordered Topic.
requirements.required_behavior: Send PUBACK packets in the order in which the corresponding PUBLISH packets were received.
requirements.why_checkable: The sentence applies the preceding PUBACK-order rule to the Server, so incoming and outgoing identifier order can be compared.

requirements.quote: When a Server processes a message that has been published to an Ordered Topic, it MUST follow the rules listed above when delivering messages to each of its subscribers.
requirements.condition: When a Server sends PUBREC packets for multiple QoS 2 PUBLISH packets associated with an Ordered Topic.
requirements.required_behavior: Send PUBREC packets in the order in which the corresponding PUBLISH packets were received.
requirements.why_checkable: The sentence applies the preceding PUBREC-order rule to the Server, so incoming and outgoing identifier order can be compared.

requirements.quote: When a Server processes a message that has been published to an Ordered Topic, it MUST follow the rules listed above when delivering messages to each of its subscribers.
requirements.condition: When a Server sends PUBREL packets after receiving multiple PUBREC packets in QoS 2 flows for an Ordered Topic.
requirements.required_behavior: Send PUBREL packets in the order in which the corresponding PUBREC packets were received.
requirements.why_checkable: The sentence applies the preceding PUBREL-order rule to the Server, so PUBREC and PUBREL identifier order can be compared.

requirements.quote: In addition it MUST send PUBLISH packets to consumers (for the same Topic and QoS) in the order that they were received from any given Client [MQTT-4.6.0-6].
requirements.condition: When a Server sends consumers multiple PUBLISH packets having the same Topic and QoS that were received from one Client.
requirements.required_behavior: Send those PUBLISH packets in the order in which that Client's packets were received.
requirements.why_checkable: Distinct messages can be published by one Client and their order at each consumer compared with Server receipt order.

requirements.quote: The rules listed above ensure that when a stream of messages is published and subscribed to with QoS 1, the final copy of each message received by the subscribers will be in the order that they were originally published in, but the possibility of message duplication could result in a re-send of an earlier message being received after one of its successor messages.
requirements.condition: When a stream is published and subscribed to at QoS 1 under the ordering rules.
requirements.required_behavior: Preserve original publication order for the final copy of each message received by subscribers.
requirements.why_checkable: A QoS 1 stream with retransmissions can be observed and the last occurrence of each message compared with publication order.

requirements.quote: The rules listed above ensure that when a stream of messages is published and subscribed to with QoS 1, the final copy of each message received by the subscribers will be in the order that they were originally published in, but the possibility of message duplication could result in a re-send of an earlier message being received after one of its successor messages.
requirements.condition: When QoS 1 duplication causes a retransmission of an earlier message after a successor has already been received.
requirements.required_behavior: Tolerate the earlier duplicate arriving after its successor while retaining the final-copy ordering guarantee.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat this permitted duplicate interleaving alone as a violation of Ordered Topic behavior.
requirements.why_checkable: A sequence such as 1,2,3,2,3,4 can be induced and receiver handling observed.

requirements.quote: If both Client and Server make sure that no more than one message is “in-flight” at any one time (by not sending a message until its predecessor has been acknowledged), then no QoS 1 message will be received after any later one - for example a subscriber might receive them in the order 1,2,3,3,4 but not 1,2,3,2,3,4.
requirements.condition: When both Client and Server limit in-flight messages to one by waiting for each predecessor's acknowledgement.
requirements.required_behavior: Prevent any QoS 1 message from being received after a later message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Allow an earlier QoS 1 message to arrive after a later message under the one-message window.
requirements.why_checkable: A QoS 1 sequence can be sent with a one-message window and all receive positions compared.

requirements.quote: Setting an in-flight window of 1 also means that order will be preserved even if the publisher sends a sequence of messages with different QoS levels on the same topic.
requirements.condition: When the in-flight window is one and a publisher sends same-topic messages with different QoS levels.
requirements.required_behavior: Preserve the publisher's message order across the different QoS levels.
requirements.why_checkable: A mixed-QoS same-topic sequence can be sent through a one-message window and delivery order compared.

requirements.quote: If present, it divides the Topic Name into multiple “topic levels”.
requirements.condition: When a topic level separator is present in a Topic Name.
requirements.required_behavior: Divide the Topic Name into separate topic levels at the separator.
requirements.why_checkable: A Topic Name with separators can be tokenized and its level boundaries compared with separator positions.

requirements.quote: A subscription’s Topic Filter can contain special wildcard characters, which allow you to subscribe to multiple topics at once.
requirements.condition: When parsing a Subscription's Topic Filter.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit valid wildcard characters that select multiple Topic Names.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reject a Topic Filter solely because it contains a valid wildcard.
requirements.why_checkable: Valid wildcard filters can be submitted and their multi-topic matching behavior observed.

requirements.quote: The wildcard characters can be used in Topic Filters, but MUST NOT be used within a Topic Name [MQTT-4.7.1-1].
requirements.condition: When constructing or accepting a Topic Name.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include either wildcard character within the Topic Name.
requirements.why_checkable: Topic Names containing each wildcard character can be submitted and checked for rejection or prevented serialization.

requirements.quote: The forward slash (‘/’ U+002F) is used to separate each level within a topic tree and provide a hierarchical structure to the Topic Names.
requirements.condition: When representing a topic level separator.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the forward slash character U+002F as the separator between topic levels.
requirements.why_checkable: The exact Unicode code point at topic-level boundaries can be inspected.

requirements.quote: Topic level separators can appear anywhere in a Topic Filter or Topic Name.
requirements.condition: When parsing a Topic Filter containing a topic level separator at any position, including the first or last position.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the separator at that position.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reject the Topic Filter solely because a separator is first, last, or otherwise positioned within it.
requirements.why_checkable: Leading, trailing, and interior separator positions can be tested independently in Topic Filters.

requirements.quote: Topic level separators can appear anywhere in a Topic Filter or Topic Name.
requirements.condition: When parsing a Topic Name containing a topic level separator at any position, including the first or last position.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the separator at that position.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reject the Topic Name solely because a separator is first, last, or otherwise positioned within it.
requirements.why_checkable: Leading, trailing, and interior separator positions can be tested independently in Topic Names.

requirements.quote: Adjacent Topic level separators indicate a zero length topic level.
requirements.condition: When two topic level separators are adjacent.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the position between them as a zero-length topic level.
requirements.why_checkable: A name or filter containing adjacent slashes can be parsed and the intervening level length checked as zero.

requirements.quote: The number sign (‘#’ U+0023) is a wildcard character that matches any number of levels within a topic. The multi-level wildcard represents the parent and any number of child levels.
requirements.condition: When matching a Topic Filter containing the multi-level wildcard.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret number sign U+0023 as matching zero or more topic levels, including the parent level itself.
requirements.why_checkable: Filters can be matched against the parent Topic Name and against names with varying numbers of child levels.

requirements.quote: The multi-level wildcard character MUST be specified either on its own or following a topic level separator.
requirements.condition: When a multi-level wildcard appears in a Topic Filter.
requirements.required_behavior: Place it either as the entire filter or immediately after a topic level separator.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Embed the multi-level wildcard after a non-separator character.
requirements.why_checkable: Standalone, slash-prefixed, and invalid embedded placements can be parsed and classified.

requirements.quote: In either case it MUST be the last character specified in the Topic Filter [MQTT-4.7.1-2].
requirements.condition: When a multi-level wildcard is present in a Topic Filter.
requirements.required_behavior: Make the wildcard the final character of the Topic Filter.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Place any character after the multi-level wildcard.
requirements.why_checkable: Filters with and without characters after # can be parsed and classified.

requirements.quote: “sport/#” also matches the singular “sport”, since # includes the parent level.
requirements.condition: When matching Topic Filter “sport/#” against Topic Name “sport”.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the Topic Name as a match because the multi-level wildcard includes the parent level.
requirements.why_checkable: The exact filter/name pair has a deterministic expected match result.

requirements.quote: “#” is valid and will receive every Application Message
requirements.condition: When a Client subscribes using Topic Filter “#”.
requirements.required_behavior: Accept the filter as valid and match it to every Application Message.
requirements.why_checkable: This non-normative example states an absolute result without defining its Topic Name scope or any exceptions, so it is incomplete as a standalone conformance check.

requirements.quote: The plus sign (‘+’ U+002B) is a wildcard character that matches only one topic level.
requirements.condition: When matching a Topic Filter containing the single-level wildcard.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret plus sign U+002B as matching exactly one topic level.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Match it across more than one topic level.
requirements.why_checkable: Candidate Topic Names spanning zero, one, and multiple separator-delimited levels can be tested.

requirements.quote: The single-level wildcard can be used at any level in the Topic Filter, including first and last levels.
requirements.condition: When a single-level wildcard is placed at any Topic Filter level, including the first or last level.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the wildcard at that level.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reject it solely because it occurs at the first or last level.
requirements.why_checkable: Filters placing + at the first, interior, and last levels can be submitted.

requirements.quote: Where it is used it MUST occupy an entire level of the filter [MQTT-4.7.1-3].
requirements.condition: When a single-level wildcard is used in a Topic Filter.
requirements.required_behavior: Make the wildcard the sole character in its topic level.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Combine the wildcard with other characters in the same topic level.
requirements.why_checkable: Whole-level and embedded + placements can be parsed and classified.

requirements.quote: It can be used at more than one level in the Topic Filter and can be used in conjunction with the multilevel wildcard.
requirements.condition: When a Topic Filter uses the single-level wildcard in more than one distinct level.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit multiple single-level wildcard occurrences.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reject an otherwise valid filter solely because + occurs at multiple levels.
requirements.why_checkable: A filter with + in multiple whole levels can be submitted and matched.

requirements.quote: It can be used at more than one level in the Topic Filter and can be used in conjunction with the multilevel wildcard.
requirements.condition: When a Topic Filter combines one or more single-level wildcards with a valid trailing multi-level wildcard.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the two wildcard kinds to be used together.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reject an otherwise valid filter solely because it combines + and #.
requirements.why_checkable: A filter such as +/# that satisfies each wildcard's placement rules can be submitted and matched.

requirements.quote: Also, because the single-level wildcard matches only a single level, “sport/+” does not match “sport” but it does match “sport/”.
requirements.condition: When matching Topic Filter “sport/+” against Topic Name “sport”.
requirements.required_behavior: Report no match because the Topic Name has no second level.
requirements.why_checkable: The exact filter/name pair has a deterministic negative match result.

requirements.quote: Also, because the single-level wildcard matches only a single level, “sport/+” does not match “sport” but it does match “sport/”.
requirements.condition: When matching Topic Filter “sport/+” against Topic Name “sport/”.
requirements.required_behavior: Report a match because the trailing separator creates one zero-length second level.
requirements.why_checkable: The exact filter/name pair has a deterministic positive match result and exercises an empty topic level.
